meta.task: Standardize how our team uses Claude Code on this repo — agent instructions, the skills and MCP servers worth adopting, and a review step — so everyone works the same way
meta.title: Standardize a Team's Claude Code Setup
meta.promptIntro: Standardize how our team uses Claude Code on this repo: agent instructions, the skills and MCP servers worth adopting, and a review step, so everyone works the same way. Prove the setup on a real task before the team commits to it, and leave it documented for whoever joins next.

nodes.label: Gather the team's needs and what exists
nodes.description: Ask what people already do by hand, what is already installed on whose machine, what may not leave the network, and what 'standardized' has to mean by when.

nodes.label: Audit the repo and how it is built
nodes.description: Read the build, the test commands, the conventions, and the parts newcomers get wrong — otherwise the instructions end up saying nothing specific.

nodes.label: Search GitHub & the blogs for candidates
nodes.description: Search GitHub, blog posts, and awesome-lists for skills and plugins that might fit this stack, collecting a long list of maybes.

nodes.label: Read READMEs repo by repo
nodes.description: Open each candidate and read its README and issues to work out what it actually does and whether it still works.

nodes.label: Judge which look-alike is the real one
nodes.description: Separate the maintained original from a thousand renamed forks and abandoned copies claiming the same feature list.

nodes.label: Try each candidate on a real task
nodes.description: Install one, run it against real work, judge whether it helped, uninstall it, and repeat — the only honest way to tell, and it costs a day.

nodes.label: Write the missing capability yourself
nodes.description: Author a skill from scratch for the thing you could not find: the instructions, the examples, the edge cases, and the rewrites after it misfires on real work.

nodes.label: Wire up the MCP servers and configs
nodes.description: Add the servers, decide project versus user scope, sort out transports and credentials, and get the same setup onto everyone's machine.

nodes.label: Write CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md by hand
nodes.description: Write the conventions, the commands and the do-nots into agent instructions — then keep rewriting them every time the repo moves, because a stale instruction file is worse than none.

nodes.label: Pilot the setup on a real task
nodes.description: Take a genuine ticket through the new setup start to finish and watch where it fights the way the team works.

nodes.label: Review what the agent produced, by hand
nodes.description: Read every diff from the pilot line by line looking for what the agent got subtly wrong — which is the whole reason nobody trusts the setup yet.

nodes.label: Friction found?
nodes.description: Did the pilot expose instructions that were wrong, missing, or quietly ignored?

nodes.label: Team agrees to adopt it
nodes.description: Walk the team through the setup and get agreement — including from whoever was never going to like it.

nodes.label: Document the setup and roll it out
nodes.description: Write the onboarding page, the per-machine setup steps, and who owns this when it breaks.

nodes.label: Standard setup adopted
nodes.description: Everyone on the team runs the same instructions, the same skills, and the same review step on this repo.

suggestions.name: K-Dense-AI/claude-skills-mcp
suggestions.claim: Vector-search over skill libraries so the right skill loads itself at the right moment.
suggestions.promptFragment: Find the candidates with K-Dense-AI/claude-skills-mcp rather than trawling GitHub, reading README after README, and guessing which look-alike repo is the real one: search the skill libraries by what the team actually needs, and let the matching skill load itself when that work comes up. Do this before anything is tried on a real task, so the shortlist arrives already narrowed.

replaceWith.label: Search the skill libraries
replaceWith.description: Vector search over the skill libraries returns the candidates worth trying — no GitHub trawl, no README-by-README read, no fork-or-original guesswork.

suggestions.name: VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills
suggestions.claim: 1,000+ ready-made skills — check here before building any capability from scratch.
suggestions.promptFragment: Before authoring any capability yourself, check VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills for one that already exists — over a thousand ready-made skills, so the gap the shortlist left is usually already filled by someone's dev team. Adopt what you find there and go straight on to wiring the servers up.

suggestions.name: langchain-ai/openwiki
suggestions.claim: Self-maintaining wiki + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md for any repo or knowledge base.
suggestions.promptFragment: Generate the agent instructions with langchain-ai/openwiki instead of writing CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md by hand and rewriting them every time the repo moves. Point it at the repo once the servers are wired, and re-run it whenever a pilot shows the instructions have drifted from the code.

replaceWith.label: Generate the agent instructions
replaceWith.description: openwiki writes and maintains CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md from the repo itself, so the files stop going stale between rewrites.

suggestions.name: openai/codex-plugin-cc
suggestions.claim: Second-model code review and task delegation — GPT checks Claude's work from inside Claude Code.
suggestions.promptFragment: Make openai/codex-plugin-cc the review step this setup is missing: after the pilot task, have it check what the agent produced from inside Claude Code, instead of reading every diff line by line yourself. Keep it in the loop afterwards so every agent change on this repo gets the same second read.

replaceWith.label: Second model reviews the agent's output
replaceWith.description: Codex checks the pilot's diffs from inside Claude Code — the standing review step, not a manual read of every line.
